# Supplementary Materials

# Supplementary Figure S1

![][image6]  
Figure S1: HPVsim Nigeria model calibration — primary goodness-of-fit diagnostic. Model output across the top-50 calibration posterior sample is overlaid on the calibration target data (black diamonds). (A) Age-specific new cervical cancer cases, 2020 — line = median across the top 50, shaded band = 2.5–97.5 percentile interval. (B) Age-specific HPV DNA prevalence, 2015 — same construction. (C) HPV genotype distribution in high-grade lesions (HSILs), 2015 — boxplots show the IQR + whiskers across the top 50. (D) HPV genotype distribution in cervical cancer, 2015 — same construction. Target data are sourced from Globocan 2020 (A) and HPV Information Centre compiled meta-analyses (B–D).

# Supplementary Figure S2

![][image7]  
Figure S2: Calibration posterior time series as a goodness-of-fit diagnostic. HPV prevalence, CIN prevalence, and age-standardized cervical cancer incidence (ASR, WHO 2000 standard) simulated from the top-50 calibration draws; solid line = median across draws, shaded band = 2.5–97.5 percentile interval across draws. The ASR panel also shows the Globocan 2020 ASR data point used as a calibration target.

# Supplementary Figure S3

![][image8]  
Figure S3: Education-uptake sensitivity — finer sweep across vaccination and screening odds ratios. Cancers averted in vaccine-targetable cohorts (birth cohorts 2015–2044, cumulative 2025–2100) relative to the status quo (S_sq: 60% aggregate adolescent coverage with vaccination OR = 5, 15% baseline screening). (A) Vaccination OR sweep — vaccination OR ∈ {2, 3, 5, 8} with aggregate coverage fixed at 60% and screening held at the 15% baseline. OR = 5 is the paper's baseline (zero by construction). (B) Screening OR sweep — screening OR ∈ {1, 2, 3, 5} at the 70% aggregate scale-up target, with vaccination held at the status-quo distribution (OR = 5, 60% aggregate). OR = 1 corresponds to the "equitable" scale-up scenario in Table 1 and OR = 3 to the "correlated" scale-up. Orange markers indicate the paper's baseline OR values; navy markers indicate the additional round-2 sweep values. Whiskers span the IQR (thick, 25th–75th percentile) and 95% uncertainty interval (thin, 2.5th–97.5th percentile) across the 50 replicates per scenario (10 calibration draws × 5 model seeds). Numeric values plotted here are reported in Supplementary Table S3.

# Supplementary Table S2

Table S2: Intervention parameters used to build each scenario in Table 1. All non-"No vaccination" scenarios share the historical 2023–2025 adolescent HPV rollout as their base program (age-9 routine at aggregate coverage 27%, 60%, 60% for 2023, 2024, 2025 respectively, plus a one-time age-10–14 catch-up in 2023 at the 2023 coverage). Scenarios diverge from 2026 onward. Vaccine product across all scenarios: quadrivalent (HPV16/18/6/11), single dose, with per-genotype sterilizing efficacy multiplied by the "efficacy at administration" column below. Screening age window: 30–50; rescreen gap: 10 years; screening test: HPV DNA. Treatment cascade for screen positives: 80% ablation + 20% excision for latent / pre-CIN / CIN states; 100% radiation for cancerous states.

*Shared constants*:

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| In-school fraction at age 9 (Nigeria) | 70% |
| Baseline (opportunistic) lifetime screening coverage in status quo | 15% (uniform) |
| Adolescent vaccine efficacy at administration | 95% (HPV16/18) |
| WHO adolescent scale-up target | 90% (in-school and out-of-school; no education gap) |
| WHO screening scale-up target | 70% lifetime coverage aggregate over the 30–50 window |
| Solved screening coverage split at 70% aggregate, education OR = 3 | in-school 77.25%, out-of-school 53.09% |
| Infant program start year (in infant delivery scenarios) | 2030 |
| Infant delivery sensitivity grid coverage levels | 60%, 75%, 90% |
| Infant delivery sensitivity grid effective-VE-at-exposure values (hypothetical) | 50%, 70%, 95% |
| Calibration draws propagated to scenarios | 10 (from top-50 calibration posterior) |
| Model seeds per calibration draw | 5 (giving 50 replicates per scenario) |

*Per-scenario intervention values from 2026 onward*:

| Scenario (as in Table 1) | Adolescent coverage (aggregate) | Adolescent split (in-school / out-of-school) | Infant program from 2030 | Infant efficacy at exposure | Screening lifetime coverage (aggregate) | Screening split (in-school / out-of-school) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No vaccination | none | — | none | — | 15% | uniform |
| Status quo | 60% | 71.4% / 33.3% (OR = 5) | none | — | 15% | uniform |
| Status quo vax with screening scale-up (correlated) | 60% | 71.4% / 33.3% (OR = 5) | none | — | 70% | 77.25% / 53.09% (OR = 3) |
| Status quo vax with screening scale-up (equitable) | 60% | 71.4% / 33.3% (OR = 5) | none | — | 70% | 70% / 70% (OR = 1) |
| WHO targets | 90% | 90% / 90% (OR = 1) | none | — | 70% | 77.25% / 53.09% (OR = 3) |
| Infant delivery, 95% efficacy | 60% (bridge 2026–2029) | 71.4% / 33.3% (bridge only) | 90% uniform + age-1–9 catch-up 2030 | 95% (hypothetical) | 70% | 77.25% / 53.09% (OR = 3) |
| Infant delivery, 70% efficacy | as row above | as row above | as row above | 70% (hypothetical) | as row above | as row above |
| Infant delivery, 50% efficacy | as row above | as row above | as row above | 50% (hypothetical) | as row above | as row above |
| Infant delivery, 60/75/90% coverage × 50/70/95% efficacy (Fig 5 grid) | 60% (bridge 2026–2029) | 71.4% / 33.3% (bridge only) | {60, 75, 90}% uniform | {50, 70, 95}% (hypothetical) | 70% | 77.25% / 53.09% (OR = 3) |
| Education-uptake sensitivity: vaccination OR ∈ {2, 3, 8} (round-2 sweep, Fig S3) | 60% | split solved for each OR at 60% aggregate | none | — | 15% | uniform |
| Education-uptake sensitivity: screening OR ∈ {2, 5} (round-2 sweep, Fig S3) | 60% | 71.4% / 33.3% (OR = 5) | none | — | 70% | split solved for each OR at 70% aggregate |

# Supplementary Table S3

Table S3: Numeric results for the education-uptake OR sensitivity sweep (source for Figure S3). Cancers averted are reported for vaccine-targetable cohorts (birth cohorts 2015–2044, cumulative 2025–2100) relative to the status quo (S_sq: 60% aggregate adolescent coverage with vaccination OR = 5, 15% baseline screening; baseline is zero by construction). Median, IQR (25th–75th percentile), and 95% uncertainty interval (2.5th–97.5th percentile) are computed across 50 replicates per scenario (10 calibration draws × 5 model seeds). Positive values indicate cancers averted relative to the status quo; negative values indicate additional cancers.

Panel A — Vaccination OR sweep (60% aggregate adolescent coverage, 15% baseline screening):

| Vaccination OR | Median | IQR (Q25–Q75) | 95% UI (Q2.5–Q97.5) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 13,647 | −2,598 to 29,523 | −35,022 to 54,485 |
| 3 | 1,895 | −14,305 to 18,530 | −39,250 to 58,826 |
| 5 (baseline) | 0 | 0 to 0 | 0 to 0 |
| 8 | −11,395 | −25,755 to −290 | −67,617 to 37,632 |

Panel B — Screening OR sweep (70% aggregate screening scale-up, vaccination held at status-quo OR = 5, 60% aggregate):

| Screening OR | Median | IQR (Q25–Q75) | 95% UI (Q2.5–Q97.5) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (equitable; matches "Status quo vaccination with screening scale-up (equitable)" in Table 1) | 152,611 | 121,148 to 189,917 | 71,020 to 221,720 |
| 2 | 141,150 | 107,579 to 160,850 | 70,728 to 189,172 |
| 3 (baseline; matches "Status quo vaccination with screening scale-up (correlated)" in Table 1) | 127,213 | 100,856 to 150,794 | 55,950 to 194,746 |
| 5 | 116,733 | 87,221 to 139,154 | 53,754 to 173,119 |

Complete implementation values (per-year vaccination probabilities computed from the aggregate coverage above, screening intervention definitions, treatment cascade probabilities) are hard-coded as module-level constants in `run_scenarios.py` in the code repository and can be reproduced from the pinned commit (`requirements.txt` pins the exact HPVsim commit used to generate the paper's numbers).
